purpose: Prove that an AI can make evidence-bearing changes to the self-hosted RCL compiler from bounded intent, rather than merely emit ordinary RCL application code.
rules: The AI receives the intent, allowed files, forbidden shortcuts, and acceptance tests.
The AI must modify RCL-owned compiler source or compiler semantics, not replace the compiler with an opaque external compiler.
Each trial must reach the native self-hosted compiler fixed point after the change.
Each trial must preserve all pre-existing fixed-point/parity/negative-control tests.
A trial is not successful until compile, execution, correctness, regression, and evidence receipts exist.
The same AI session may not invent a mutation, reveal its oracle patch to itself, restore the known original, and count that as an independent success.
At least one trial must be generated from an independently specified change request or hidden mutation whose oracle repair is unavailable to the generating AI.
AI_GENERATE is a reproducibility gate, not a declaration that prior AI-assisted development probably occurred.

trials.intent: Extend or repair one general expression/compiler behavior in the RCL-owned compiler while preserving byte-identical self-host fixed point and existing semantics.
forbidden: self-invent trivial mutation and restore known original

trials.intent: Add or repair a general parser/lowering capability in the RCL-owned compiler and demonstrate that the capability works on at least two structurally distinct source fixtures.
Repair a deliberately introduced compiler mutation using only the failing evidence and compiler sources, then restore fixed-point, parity and rejection behavior.
